newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriots to step up checkpoint protest.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriots to step up checkpoint protest.

text.p: Greek Cypriots said on Thursday they would intensify protests at a U.N. checkpoint after Turkish Cypriot authorities imposed crossing restrictions on their side of the "green line" dividing the capital.

The Turkish Cypriot administration banned the crossing of Greek Cypriots and members of the Maronite community on Wednesday in response to three straight weekends of protests by Greek Cypriots at the checkpoint to discourage tourist visits to the northern part of the island, occupied by Turkey since 1974.

The closure sparked an angry reaction from the Cypriot government, which controls the majority Greek Cypriot populated south, but appeared to strengthen the resolve of organisers to step up their protests.
"We will be there every day...We will start at the weekend and onwards," Greek Cypriot MP Marios Matsakis, who started the protests, told Reuters. "It will be even stronger."

The Turkish Cypriot move affects some 500 Greek Cypriots living in the Karpasia peninsula and 187 Maronites, who belong to a branch of the Roman Catholic church in the Middle East, living at a village on the north western coast of the island.
United Nations officials said they were seeking clarifications from the Turkish Cypriot administration over the checkpoint closure.
"We will protest any obstacles imposed," U.N. spokesman Waldemar Rokozsewski said.
Greek Cypriot families visiting the south were barred access to their homes in the north on Wednesday as they were returning.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded and occupied its northern third in 1974 following a short-lived coup in Nicosia engineered by the military ruling Greece. The breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north is recognised only by Turkey.
